analyst_view.overall: Granada have won five league games in a row under Pacheta but have not played in the league since 1 November because their home game with Tenerife was postponed. Las Palmas have won two straight under Albert Sánchez, the latest 2-0 at home to Eldense with both goals (Álex Suárez and Betancor) in stoppage time, per one match roundup. I found little fresh team news this week; no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I have moved from lower to same: Granada's run was built on narrow wins, but their league games average close to three goals (20-14 in 12) and Las Palmas's just over three (19-21 in 13). Nothing in the news points clearly either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners and I keep it there. Granada are happy without the ball (4,574 passes in 12 games by LaLiga's count, against 5,955 for Las Palmas), so their 5.2 may be a little high, but Las Palmas should get more than 3.9 if they have most of the ball.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and I see no clear push either way. LaLiga has Granada on just 22 yellows and no reds in 12 games and Las Palmas on 34 and two, which the site's split already reflects.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots, with Granada expected to take 14.4. I lean slightly lower: Granada win through efficiency rather than volume, and LaLiga counts Las Palmas at only 106 shots in 13 games. Two weeks without a league game may also blunt Granada's sharpness.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Granada had few efforts on target in their win at Elda, and Las Palmas needed stoppage time to break down Eldense last week. Jesé is Las Palmas's top scorer with four.
